findings.claim: escalate.verify/apply will publish non-null start/end on an item whose status is `missing` or `omitted`, violating the output contract, and nothing in the gate can see it.
findings.evidence: escalate.py:147 `flagged = {i['item'] for i in items}` admits every item including non-span-bearing ones; escalate.py:200-225 `apply()` writes start/end/method but leaves `status` alone (ADR-036 §j). specs/001-sec10k-contract.md:78: 'For status: missing / omitted: start/end are null — there is no span.' `envelope_shape` never asserts that rule, so the malformed envelope is green. The same envelope's `meta.coverage` is recomputed at extract.py:333 over `i.get('start') is not None`, so a resolved `missing` item silently inflates the very coverage number the D8 trigger and the whole D11 cost argument rest on. This is the shape of the named exam document: `c-2025` is 21 `missing` + 2 `omitted`.
findings.repro: see pr58-r1 repro block — verify() accepts a proposal for a `missing` item (title_similarity 0.955, rejections []), apply() then writes start=11552 end=16945 method=llm_localize with status still 'missing'
findings.acceptance: `verify` rejects any proposed code whose item is not in eval_adapter.SPAN_STATUSES (or `apply` also moves status, with an ADR ruling for that), AND `envelope_shape` gains the missing/omitted null-span assertion so the rule is enforced rather than documented, AND an adversarial case covers a proposal naming a `missing` item, watched red first.

findings.claim: The 'all-or-nothing' safety property ADR-036 §b and verify()'s docstring both publish is false: verify partially applies a proposal in which some spans failed a check.
findings.evidence: ADR-036:96 '**All-or-nothing.** Either every proposed span survives or none is used.' and escalate.py:120 same claim. The loop at escalate.py:149-176 `continue`s past each failing entry, accumulating survivors in `merged`, and returns `merged` whenever non-empty (:178-179). Only INV-S1 failures at :185 discard the whole proposal. `_demo` never covers it: every mixed proposal it constructs happens to trip INV-S1 as a side effect, so the property has never been watched.
findings.repro: verify(text, items, {'8':[b,b+len(b8)], '1':[0,40]}) -> ({'8': {...}}, ['item 1: 40 chars < SPAN_FLOOR 1500 ...']) — item 8 applied anyway
findings.acceptance: Either verify returns ({}, why) whenever `why` is non-empty for any non-null proposed span, or ADR-036 §b:96 and escalate.py:120 are rewritten to say what the code does; either way an adversarial case pins the chosen semantics with a mixed proposal, watched red first.

findings.claim: ADR-036 names escalate.py::_demo and llm.py::_demo as 'Enforced by' artifacts, but neither the pre-commit hook nor CI runs them — the entire trust boundary and money ceiling can be deleted with the gate 100% green.
findings.evidence: ADR-036:19 lists both under **Enforced by**. ci.yml runs the other module self-checks but no `src.sec10k.escalate` and no `src.sec10k.llm`; .githooks/pre-commit runs only evals.run --suite fast + two bench checks. No eval case reaches verify()/apply(): `escalation-trigger-quiet` returns at route()'s quiet branch (:243), `escalation-no-credential` breaks at the EscalationUnavailable handler (:271). ci.yml:31-36 already carries this repo's own ruling (PR #25 R1): 'A self-check no job runs is a claim, not enforcement.'
findings.repro: Replace the SIM_FLOOR / SPAN_FLOOR / INV-S1 guards with `if False:` and both Budget guards likewise -> invariant 75/75 and fast 138/138 stay GREEN; only `python3 -m src.sec10k.escalate` catches it.
findings.acceptance: `python3 -m src.sec10k.escalate` and `python3 -m src.sec10k.llm` are added to the unit-tests job in .github/workflows/ci.yml (where ADR-026/029/032/033's self-checks were wired), and re-running the mutation turns that job red.

findings.claim: ADR-036 §d4's headline '$3.4 per dev sweep, roughly 60x' is not re-derivable from the ADR's own cost model, and its document list contradicts the ADR's own census two sections earlier.
findings.evidence: ADR-036:276-280 says routing on item_span_near_empty 'would escalate 12 of 43 dev documents, including jpm-2024 and bac-2006, for an estimated $3.4 per dev sweep — roughly 60x'. But §c3 states 'only bac-2006 is silent', and the independent census confirms bac-2006 is NOT among the 12. Re-deriving with the ADR's own model reproduces every §d1 figure to the published digit, then gives a 12-document sweep of $4.7032 = ~85x, not $3.4/60x. No subset reaches $3.4. The ADR itself says of this figure 'That number is the argument.'
findings.repro: 12-doc sweep recomputed from ADR §d1's own model -> $4.7032, ratio 84.6x vs the published 3.4/60x
findings.acceptance: §d4 publishes a figure that reproduces from the §d1 model and the §c1 census, with arithmetic shown as §d1 does, and drops bac-2006 from the escalating set — or names the different assumption that produces $3.4.

findings.claim: The reason ADR-036 gives for keeping A2 declined attributes to D9 a ruling D9 did not make over five of the nine filings involved, and describes items 7/8 as 'disagreed' when ADR-034 says they were never adjudicated.
findings.evidence: ADR-036:145 'The nine real filings item_span_near_empty hits are the A2 class ... which D9 declined', echoed at escalate.py:44-48. ADR-034 §d1 enumerates A2 as exactly five filings (cvx-2015, jpm-2024, bac-2006, ge-1994, spatz-2014). Only four of the nine are members; xom-2021, ko-1997, nvda-2024, reac-2015, sandston-2021 were never in D9's scope. Separately §c3's replacement reason rests on ADR-034 §e2 reason 1, whose text reads: 'the extraction-auditor's blind sample adjudicated cvx-2015 item 6 ... CORRECT. Items 7 and 8 were never independently adjudicated.' The flag reaches items 1/7/8, never item 6.
findings.repro: sed -n '143,150p' ADR-036; grep -n 'never independently adjudicated' ADR-034
findings.acceptance: §c1 reason 3, §c3 and the escalate.py comment either narrow the claim to the four filings actually in ADR-034's A2 set (naming the other five as an unruled population), or state plainly that items 7/8 are unadjudicated rather than disagreed. The ruling can stand; its cited evidence must match ADR-034's text.

findings.claim: `Budget` is a per-document ceiling, not the 'per-run' ceiling its docstring claims, and the paid path is reachable unauthenticated on the deployed inspector — so nothing bounds aggregate spend.
findings.evidence: llm.py:85-86 'A per-run ceiling on paid work'. But escalate.py:247 constructs a fresh Budget inside every route() call and no caller passes one: extract.py:129 defaults budget=None, app.py:139 calls extract_items(..., escalate=escalate) with no budget. So the ceiling is 2 calls / $1.00 PER DOCUMENT; a 43-fixture escalate=True sweep has a ceiling of 43x that. ADR-036 §d3 discloses only the one-call overshoot, reading as if $1.00 were the run ceiling. Compounding: escalate is wired to all three public endpoints (app.py:178 fixture, :206 ?escalate=1 upload, :239 url), README.md:8 advertises a live deployment, and app.py has no auth, no rate limit, no aggregate budget (only MAX_BYTES 25MB at :37). If a credential is ever set on that host, an anonymous caller can drive unbounded ~$1.5 opus-class calls by uploading collapsed filings. No ADR section, README line or debt row mentions this.
findings.repro: grep -n 'per-run ceiling' src/sec10k/llm.py; grep -n 'budget = budget if budget is not None' src/sec10k/escalate.py; grep -nE 'Depends|Authorization|rate.?limit' src/sec10k/web/app.py -> no matches
findings.acceptance: Either a run/process-level budget is threaded through extract_items (one Budget per sweep, one per server process for the web layer), or llm.Budget's docstring and ADR-036 §d3 are corrected to say 'per document' and a debt row records the deployment exposure — plus an explicit statement of whether the deployed inspector may ever hold a credential.

findings.claim: verify()'s docstring check 1 claims a stricter guard than the code implements — it accepts any item of the document, not only ones the trigger flagged.
findings.evidence: escalate.py:113-115 claims 'one the trigger actually flagged'. Implementation at :147 is `flagged = {i['item'] for i in items}` — the whole item list, no reference to trigger()['items'] or the `codes` the rung was asked about (:248). ADR-036 §b1 states the weaker property correctly, so this is the code comment, not the ADR. It is also the mechanism R1 rides on.
findings.acceptance: Either verify takes the flagged/asked set and enforces it, or the docstring's second clause is deleted so it matches ADR-036 §b1.
